The bible uses the natural things of nature to illustrate many things, like the seeds we sow, and this illustration of us being the branches, and Jesus being the vine. We should not ever try to operate on our own, as like a branch, we need the vine (Jesus) to provide all our nourishment. In our busy lives, many don’t think it is possible to always abide in Jesus, but you can by bringing every thought into obedience to Him (2 Corinthians 10:5). If we can go through the whole day worrying about a problem, then we can keep our minds upon Jesus all day. How true it is that we can do nothing without Jesus – but thank God I am never without Him (Hebrews 13:5).

The way that we abide in Jesus is to obey His commandments (Hebrews 5:9), and follow His direction given us through the Holy Spirit. For those of you who don't know, a living dex is where you have your PC full of every single Pokemon. For instance, Box 1 starts with Bulbasaur, Ivysaur, Venusaur, Charmander, etc. That way, each time a new game is released, you can just migrate them all and have the Pokedex completed. I have taken it one step further by acquiring each and every one myself, without trading. All caught or bred by me.

I think it started in the days of Heart Gold. I sank so many hours into that game that eventually all I had left to do was the Pokedex. I didn't complete it by the time Black came out, so I migrated and completed it there. Repeat for X version. I still don't have that diploma because I'm lazy.

I completed it the first time in X last year. It was very interesting feeling, as the closest I had been before was gen 1 (1 eeveelution and 2 others) and 2 (Celebi, 2 eeveelutions, 3 others). It was very frustrating living in remote places and therefore couldn't find people to trade with or go to events for those special giveaways.

Now that Pokémon is online, it's crazy easy. I actually managed to fill many of my spaces by the random power of WT. Many breeders such as myself use the WT to send out our imperfect 3-5IV Pokémon. For the harder ones I then went to online trading threads to exchange with other trainers around the world. And for the final, final mons (I remember Arceus being one of them) I managed to finish that at a convention by doing trade backs and paid those people with shinys for their time.

Pokémon is a social game. How social you are (and lucky enough to find those with the mons you are missing) determines how fast you can finish your dex.
